- When sentiment drops below 0.5 in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or shift downward.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent dip, but true outcome shows sharp drop or volatility, cap forecast growth or introduce early correction.
- After a spike in sentiment (e.g., >0.8), model often overshoots; apply downward bias or reduce slope after peak sentiment.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., after high, price drops), model often fails to adjust; add lagged mean reversion term or reduce forecast momentum.
- When sentiment is flat or negative, model tends to overreact; dampen forecast volatility or use sentiment as a smoothing factor.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period; consider anchoring forecast to recent 7-14 day average if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows multiple 0.00 entries, model tends to ignore sentiment and overpredict; apply sentiment-weighted decay to forecast.
